what: Dream drove the real right Maker Arm from the MacBook: Saleh's water-bottle prompt, live arm cameras and measured joints in, Dream action chunks out through pickup_server's guarded moves.
why: First physical Dream-controlled motion: the step before moving the same loop to the Jetson.
details: Five closed-loop cycles, Dream get_action about 0.6 s each (dream-1-beta): the arm panned toward the bottle and reached down and out (shoulder -101, elbow 71, wrist 54 SDK deg) with the jaws opening. No grasp: the elbow motor reached the 52 C guard mid-reach (it started at 47 C after the day's use); pickup_server froze and the loop's rest returned the arm home and released it (return verified).
Every exit returns home via rest; targets are clamped 2 deg inside the SDK profile limits (the dry run caught a shoulder target the server would refuse); speed is pickup_server's 15 deg/s cap.
Mac dashboard reads the three arm cameras by local index (--arm-cams devices:1,2,0) and the MacBook webcam as the perception view.
Dream warned that the tool centre point is hand-set (uncalibrated) and that a person should confirm the camera inputs with dream.check / dream.input_check before real runs.
Next: cool the motors below about 40 C before retrying; heat, not Dream latency, limits the reach.
